Reaching diverse communities
Why ElevenLabs
Impact and results
What's next
Learn More
Contact Sales
Beam serves frontline social services teams across five countries, supporting more than 130,000 meetings a week across UK Local Government alone.
Beam deployed three ElevenLabs capabilities across their platform:
ElevenAgents:
A 24/7 phone line to give access to services and routing high-priority cases to human caseworkers.
Transcription:
Compliant meeting documentation generated in seconds after each meeting.
Translation:
Real-time multilingual support so people receiving services aren't blocked by language barriers.
Unmute
Always-on support for people who can't wait until morning
Social services teams are overwhelmed with demand during working hours, and unavailable outside them. Someone in need of support outside of office hours or in the middle of the night would have to leave a message, waiting hours or days for support.
Beam deployed ElevenAgents so people can access time-critical social services at any time of day or night. Informed by comprehensive locally relevant guidance, law and regulation, the agent holds a conversation, assesses the level of risk, labels it, and flags high-priority cases for a human caseworker to prioritize during working hours. Lower-risk conversations are still captured and documented, so nothing is lost, with routine enquiries resolved immediately for the service user.
Now we're able to provide a voice agent for people who need support 24/7, transforming access to services. The AI can understand the risk of those conversations, label it, and make sure that if it's a high-risk situation, a human being can pick it up first thing in the morning.
— Alex Stephany, Founder and CEO, Beam
Freeing frontline workers from documentation
Documentation is essential for compliance and continuity of care, but it consumes a significant share of a social worker's day. As Stephany puts it, “that's not why people get into this sector”.
Beam uses ElevenLabs transcription to generate compliant documentation in seconds after a meeting ends. With frontline teams juggling dozens of cases every week, that time savings adds up.
This is technology that is taking the grunt-work out of social services, liberating tens of thousands of critical frontline workers in the UK and around the world to connect with and support other human beings.
— Alex Stephany, Founder and CEO, Beam
Reaching diverse communities
Beam serves diverse communities where multiple languages are spoken. Beam uses ElevenLabs translation to democratize access to social service, no matter the language, so everyone can get access to services without delays or drop-off. In critical care moments, it’s key to have a system that understands and can respond to the nuances and idioms of different languages and dialects.
Why ElevenLabs
Beam operates in an environment where safety, security, and emotional nuance are imperative. The agent needs to be able to connect with customers naturally, be emotionally sensitive, and leave no margin for error on security.
ElevenLabs' vertically integrated stack keeps latency low and voice quality high because
STT
, LLM, and
TTS
run in one colocated system. Voices and conversations feel natural even in high urgency or sensitive contexts. Beam also leverages Guardrails in ElevenAgents to manage risk throughout conversations, making sure the Agent stays within safe boundaries no matter how a call unfolds. And as Beam expands, support for 70+ languages and localized voices means agents can sound natural in each new community.
You want to speak to an agent that understands your idiom and can interpret your emotion, and there is no margin for error when it comes to security and safety.
— Alex Stephany, Founder and CEO, Beam
Impact and results
ElevenLabs enabled Beam to extend its platform with transcription, translation, and voice agent capabilities that drive measurable results:
50%+ reduction in call handling time,
with agents providing access to services and routing high-priority cases to human caseworkers
20% of frontline worker time saved
through compliant meeting docs generated in seconds, freeing teams for direct service
24/7, 365 service availability,
which was previously limited to business hours only
At the end of the day, this is technology that creates space for humanity in social services.
— Alex Stephany, Founder and CEO, Beam
What's next
As Beam expands into new regions, their focus is on providing world-leading capabilities that empower millions of frontline workers while staying localized, making sure each community receives the human-centered support they deserve.

AI technology restores Ben Baldanza’s communication abilities post-ALS diagnosis

On this page
Introduction
Ben Baldanza
, the former CEO of Spirit Airlines, known for his dynamic leadership, faced a new challenge when diagnosed with ALS in 2022.
The disease progressively impaired his motor skills and significantly affected his speech, making his ongoing work as a board observer, teacher, writer, and podcaster a challenge. Rather than step back, Ben and his wife, Marcia Baldanza, went looking for AI solutions that could help preserve his voice as the disease progressed.
Collaborating with the nonprofit Bridging Voice and ElevenLabs, they aimed to recreate Ben's voice using samples from his time as a podcast host.
We used over 200 podcast episodes to create a professional AI clone of Ben’s voice that mirrored his original tone and clarity. This new voice debuted to much acclaim, allowing Ben to continue hosting his podcast with a voice his audience knows and loves.
To hear the difference, listen to this episode of Airline Confidential before Ben cloned his voice:
And the episode that aired after Ben turned to ElevenLabs:
The feedback from the listeners has been overwhelmingly positive, with many expressing support for Ben's continued presence in the podcast. Importantly, Ben’s AI voice lets him not only maintain his professional roles but also enhances his daily interactions, giving him a tool to express himself authentically despite ALS.
Ben shared his excitement with our team, writing,
"Words can't express how thrilled I am with the voice clone you created for me. I've been telling everyone about this and shouting ElevenLabs' praises from the rooftops!"
Ben's story is another testament to the power of technology to profoundly contribute to people’s accessibility needs and wellbeing. His optimism and determination, coupled with innovative AI solutions, have allowed him to face his challenges head-on, continuing to lead a fulfilling life that inspires others.

November 29th, 2024, Global - Bertelsmann, a leading media, services and education company based in Europe, has partnered with ElevenLabs to use AI in creating new stories and experiences across its brands. ElevenLabs’ AI

Currently, 36 companies within the Bertelsmann Group use ElevenLabs’ technology, gaining improved production timelines and broader creative possibilities. The partnership reflects a shared goal: using AI to help creators do what they do best, not to replace them.

In AAA game development, audio design is the unsung hero behind every immersive experience. But what are the tools favored by industry giants? And will new AI-backed software be shaking up the leader board?
We’ve taken a deep dive into the world of pro
sound effects
generation. Let's unlock the secrets behind the audio magic that makes AAA games so successful.
Key takeaways
AAA video games are top-tier titles developed by large studios with high production values and complex gameplay mechanics.
Sound effect tools are crucial in creating immersive audio experiences for AAA games.
AI-driven innovators like ElevenLabs are developing professional audio generation which has revolutionized the video game landscape.
Developers should consider factors like integration with game engines, ease of use, and licensing costs when choosing sound effects tools.
What are AAA video games? Definition and examples
AAA
video games
are developed by large, established studios with substantial budgets and resources. These games typically feature high production values, expansive worlds, advanced graphics, and complex gameplay mechanics.
They become household names and make billions of dollars worldwide - 2023’s blockbusters were “Hogwarts Legacy”, “Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare III”, and “Madden NFL 24”. AAA games often set industry standards and push the boundaries of what gaming technology can achieve.
Strategies for using sound effect tools in AAA game development
AAA game developers utilize a variety of sophisticated
sound effects
tools to create immersive and dynamic audio experiences for players. These tools range from industry-standard software to custom-built engines tailored to the specific needs of each game.
Sound designers meticulously craft soundscapes using a combination of recorded audio, synthesized effects, and procedural generation techniques. For example, in "Half-Life: Alyx" (Valve Corporation), developers utilized spatial audio technology to heighten immersion in the virtual reality experience.
Now, AI tools like ElevenLabs are hugely speeding up the game development process with their advanced
sound effect generation
capabilities. Tools such as the
Soundboard
allow designers to instantly preview and apply a wide range of categorized SFX, helping teams prototype and refine soundscapes faster than ever.
The top 6 AAA video game sound effect tools
Below, we've ranked some of the top AAA video game sound effects tools for AAA video game developers, digging into their features, pros, and cons.
1. FMOD
FMOD audio software is a comprehensive middleware solution for interactive audio design in video games.
Top features
Intuitive interface for easy implementation of complex soundscapes and dynamic audio systems.
Comprehensive library of sound effects and plugins for versatility and creative freedom.
Integration with popular game engines such as Unity and Unreal Engine streamlines the workflow for developers.
Pros
Powerful features tailored for interactive audio design, ideal for AAA game development.
Versatile and customizable, allowing developers to create immersive audio experiences.
Seamless integration with game engines enhances efficiency and productivity.
Cons
Licensing fees may be prohibitive for smaller studios with limited budgets.
Extensive capabilities may overwhelm beginners or those with simpler audio needs.
2. Wwise
Wwise is a sophisticated audio solution widely used in the gaming industry, offering developers extensive tools for creating dynamic and immersive soundscapes that seamlessly integrate with game engines.
Top features
Advanced authoring tools for creating interactive audio experiences with ease.
Robust audio pipeline management, allowing for efficient organization and implementation of audio assets.
Real-time profiling and monitoring tools for fine-tuning audio performance and debugging.
Pros
Extensive integration with game engines like Unity and Unreal Engine, facilitating seamless workflow integration.
Comprehensive audio middleware solution with a wide range of features for AAA game development.
Cons
Steeper learning curve compared to some other audio tools, requiring time and dedication to master.
Limited built-in sound libraries compared to some competitors, necessitating additional resources for asset creation.
Occasional compatibility issues with certain game engines or platforms may arise, requiring troubleshooting.
3. ElevenLabs
ElevenLabs presents a range of AI audio design tools to enhance AAA games. Along with a vast
voice library
and a neat
dubbing studio
, ElevenLabs has recently teased a cutting-edge
sound effect generator
that utilizes TTS (Text-To-Speech). What's more, if you need
male
,
female
,
angry
,
seductive
, or
screaming
voices on top of sound effects, ElevenLabs has you covered.
Top features
Cutting-edge AI sound effects.
All of ElevenLab’s tools are fully end-to-end automated, saving developers huge amounts of work
Pros
The SFX generator offers a wide range of parameters for finetuning sound effects, including pitch, amplitude, duration, and modulation.
ElevenLabs generates crystal clear audio (128 kbps), well suited for the most illustrious AAA games
Generating sound effects in real-time eliminates the need for scouring libraries, saving developers valuable time and streamlining the game development process.
Wide variety of high quality sounds:
Gun sound effect
Alarm sound effect
DJ scratch sound effect
Phone ringing sound effect
Clock sound effect
Camera sound effect
3. Nuendo
Nuendo is a professional digital audio workstation (DAW) known for its advanced audio editing and mixing capabilities, commonly used in music and post-production but also leveraged by some game developers for its high-quality audio recording and processing features.
Top features
Advanced audio editing and mixing capabilities with industry-standard tools for precise control over audio elements.
High-quality audio recording and processing features, suitable for capturing and manipulating audio assets for game development.
Comprehensive support for surround sound formats and immersive audio technologies, enabling developers to create immersive audio experiences.
Pros
Established software widely used in professional audio production, ensuring reliability and stability.
Extensive plugin support and integration with third-party audio tools, allowing for customization and expansion of functionality.
Cons
Primarily designed for music and post-production workflows, lacking some features specifically tailored for interactive audio design.
Limited integration with game engines compared to dedicated audio middleware solutions like FMOD and Wwise.
4. Logic
Logic audio software is renowned for its robust features and intuitive interface, making it a popular choice among musicians and producers for audio editing. It’s also used by some big game studios.
Top features
Comprehensive digital audio workstation (DAW) functionality with advanced recording, editing, and mixing tools.
Extensive library of virtual instruments and audio effects, offering a wide range of creative possibilities for music composition and production.
Seamless integration with macOS ecosystem and hardware, providing a streamlined workflow for Mac-based game development.
Pros
Established software with a strong reputation in the
music
production industry, ensuring reliability and stability.
Versatile audio processing capabilities, suitable for both music composition and sound design for games.
Cons
Primarily designed for music production workflows, lacking some features specifically tailored for interactive audio design in games.
Limited integration with game engines compared to dedicated audio middleware solutions like FMOD and Wwise.
5. Houdini
Houdini is a powerful procedural content creation software often used in the gaming industry. It allows developers to create dynamic and adaptive soundscapes within games through its integration with game engines like Unreal Engine and Unity.
Top features
Powerful procedural audio generation tools for creating dynamic and adaptive soundscapes within games.
Extensive support for procedural content creation, enabling developers to generate vast amounts of audio assets efficiently.
Integration with game engines like Unreal Engine and Unity, allowing for seamless integration of procedural audio into game environments.
Pros
A unique approach to audio design with a focus on procedural generation, providing innovative solutions for game developers.
Scalable and customizable workflows, suitable for projects of various sizes and complexities.
Active community and extensive documentation for learning and support.
Cons
Steeper learning curve compared to traditional audio tools, requiring familiarity with procedural workflows and scripting languages.
Limited adoption in the game development industry compared to more established audio middleware solutions like FMOD and Wwise.
Less specialized focus on interactive audio design, potentially requiring additional workarounds for specific game audio requirements.
Choosing the best sound effect tools for game development
Choosing the right sound effect tools is vital for AAA game studios striving for top-tier audio experiences. Developers must consider project needs, including complexity, fidelity, and platform requirements.
Industry-standard software like FMOD and Wwise offers comprehensive features for interactive audio design, while new AI-backed software like ElevenLabs offers more creative potential with synthetic sound and audio
cloning
.
Custom-built engines or middleware solutions may provide tailored solutions for specific mechanics or challenges. For instance, "God of War" by Santa Monica Studio utilized a mix of proprietary tools and middleware for its cinematic audio experience.
Ensuring compatibility with existing pipelines and integration with game engines is also crucial. Ultimately, selecting tools aligned with the project's vision and technical needs is paramount for AAA studios aiming for unparalleled audio immersion.
Final thoughts
The world of AAA video game sound effect tools is diverse, offering a range of options tailored to different project needs and developer preferences.
While FMOD and Wwise are widely recognized as industry standards, newer entrants like ElevenLabs and Houdini bring innovative approaches to interactive audio design. ElevenLabs is a particularly powerful option, catering to all voice requirements on top of sound effects, whether you need
sultry
,
creepy
,
strange
,
nasally
, or
baritone
voices.
Each tool has its strengths and weaknesses, so developers should carefully evaluate their requirements and consider factors such as integration with game engines, ease of use, and licensing costs.
Regardless of the tool chosen, the ultimate goal is to create immersive audio experiences that enhance gameplay and captivate players, making sound effects tools an essential component of AAA game development.

AAA video games represent the highest quality and budget in the gaming industry, developed by major studios. They often feature advanced graphics, complex gameplay, and high production values, setting industry standards.

Sound effect tools are crucial for creating immersive audio experiences in AAA games, significantly enhancing gameplay and player engagement by providing realistic and dynamic soundscapes.

Industry-standard tools like FMOD and Wwise are widely used due to their comprehensive features for interactive audio design. Innovations like ElevenLabs introduce AI-driven audio capabilities, offering fresh approaches to sound creation.

FMOD and Wwise have established middleware solutions with robust audio management features, while ElevenLabs leverages AI to provide more versatile and quick audio creation, particularly useful in localization and procedural generation.
What factors should developers consider when choosing sound effect tools?
Developers should evaluate integration with game engines, ease of use, licensing costs, and the specific audio needs of their project. Compatibility with existing pipelines and the tool's feature set are also critical considerations.

The audiobook market has evolved beyond Audible's credit-based model. Today's listeners want flexibility in format, pricing, and content. Here are the top platforms challenging Audible's dominance, each offering unique advantages for audiobook enthusiasts.

FAQs
Given people’s busy schedules,
AI audiobooks
are becoming increasingly popular among young and seasoned readers alike.
Authors and ebook publishers can tap into this market to increase book sales and make more revenue.
If you’re planning to self-publish an audiobook, this guide will help you familiarize yourself with the major audiobook publishing platforms and their advantages and disadvantages.
Tap into the growing audiobook market
In our digital age, audiobooks have taken the literary industry by storm. Providing a practical alternative to traditional reading, their popularity has grown massively as modern life continues to get busier.
Literary connoisseurs and reading enthusiasts worldwide rely on audiobooks to entertain themselves during traveling and daily commutes, relax, or preserve healthy vision and avoid eye strain.
Likewise, readers with vision-related problems can enjoy their favorite novels and non-fiction works, making audiobooks an accessible alternative to traditional paperbacks and hardcovers - a feat that is becoming more popular thanks to the ease by which audiobooks can be generated with AI tools.
Whether you're planning on self-publishing your
AI audiobook
or partnering with publishing companies to assist you with the process, choosing the right platform for audiobook publishing and distribution can make or break audiobook sales and success.
In this article, we dive into several well-known and niche audiobook publishing and distribution platforms. Keep reading to explore your options and choose from the best audiobook publishing companies and platforms available.
The best audiobook publishing companies and platforms
With so many audiobook publishing platforms to choose from, deciding on a single platform may seem overwhelming. To help you make an informed decision, we have compiled a list of audiobook publishing platforms, from the most popular options like Amazon's Audiobook Creation Exchange (ACX) to niche options like Scribe Media. Note that their policies around use of AI narration are evolving so you should consult any platforms terms of service before uploading, particularly in regard to the use of AI narration and text to speech.
Without further ado, let's dive into the best audiobook production companies and publishing companies on the web!
Amazon's Audiobook Creation Exchange (ACX)
Amazon's Audiobook Creation Exchange (ACX) audiobook distribution platform is undeniably an industry leader. ACX connects authors, publishers, and professional narrators, providing audiobook production, publishing, and distribution services under one roof.
Pros

ACX possesses a vast market share, opening you up to a wider audience. It distributes audiobooks to Audible, Amazon, and iTunes, allowing you to access audiobook enthusiasts on all three platforms. It's the largest audiobook store on the market, with over 200,000 titles available to audiobook listeners.
Likewise, ACX allows you to upload ready audio files or produce your own audiobook directly through the platform (for instance, by assisting you with professional narration by helping you hire an ACX professional narrator).
Cons
Under their current policy
, ACX/Audible does not allow the publishing of audiobooks narrated by
AI voices
. This means you will not be able to publish your ElevenLabs audiobook there.
Although ACX has many benefits, publishing your audiobook on this platform has drawbacks. Firstly, publishing your audiobook on major audiobook platforms like ACX opens you up to significant competition.
Moreover, higher royalty rates (40%) on ACX require exclusivity, meaning your audiobooks can only be distributed to Audible, Amazon, and iTunes. If you're not exclusive with the platform, authors only receive 25%.
Findaway Voices
Another industry leader in the audiobook industry, Findaway Voices, provides all the essential services to self-published authors to reach a wide audience and boost audiobook sales. Independent audiobook publishers can find everything they need at Findaway Voices.
Pros
Findaway Voices is an excellent self-publishing platform. With no exclusivity required, the audiobook publishing platform allows you to distribute your audiobook to a broader range of retailers and reach more listeners.
Likewise, audiobook authors are given control over critical aspects such as audiobook prices. They also receive 80% of the 25% royalties from Audible, Amazon, and iTunes at a non-exclusive rate and 80% of the 40-50% royalties from other retailers.
Cons
Although Findaway Voices provides authors with a vast distribution network, it doesn't have the same visibility as platforms like Audible. Additionally, some consider the platform's pricing structure complex.
Kobo Writing Life
Kobo is a well-known Canadian ebook, audiobook, e-reader, and tablet retailer. Regarding audiobook publishing, the company also has an ebook and audiobook platform called "Kobo Writing Life" - a helpful and comprehensive platform for self-publishers and independent authors.
Pros
Kobo Writing Life may not have reached industry giant status just yet, but it's growing rapidly, generating over 150% more book sales in 2023 compared to 2022.
Regarding distribution strategy, Kobo Writing Life lists your book on the main Kobo platform, as well as Walmart, Indigo (Canada's top bookstore), and Bol.
Regarding royalties, Kobo's structure is relatively simple: 35% royalties for audiobooks priced $2.99 or lower, 45% royalties for audiobooks priced over $2.99, and 32% for specific subscription customers.
Cons
While Kobo is growing rapidly, it has a considerably smaller audiobook market share compared to industry giants like Amazon and Audible. It also has a limited audiobook catalog, and audiobook marketing and promotional tools are limited.
Google Play Books
Alongside thousands of other services, Google also offers self-publishing options for ebooks and audiobooks via Google Play Books, allowing audiobook authors to tap into a giant market.
Pros
As a Google sub-service, Google Play Books has a massive reach, especially considering that the Google Play Store comes pre-installed on every Android device. Reach customers in over 40 countries, receive 50% royalties with distributors like Publish Drive, and benefit from non-exclusive publishing.
Cons
Google may be an industry leader, but its audiobook section is smaller than that of publisher-only platforms. Regarding revenue share, some authors may prefer flat royalty rates offered by other platforms compared to Google Play Books' revenue share model. Lastly, marketing and promotional tools are also limited.
Author's Republic
Known as a user-friendly platform among audiobook enthusiasts and publishers, Author's Republic is a staple choice for audiobook publishing and distribution.
Providing access to major retailers and libraries, transparent royalty rates, and advanced analytics tools, Author's Republic is an excellent choice for publishers looking to upload and distribute audiobooks and track performance.
Pros
Author's Republic offers transparent royalty rates, with authors typically receiving 35-70% of the list price. Royalties depend on distribution channels and pricing models, allowing you to choose from several options.
Other pros include a vast distribution network and non-exclusive distribution for more flexibility and selling options.
Cons
Like the other publishing platforms listed above, Author's Republic provides limited promotional tools and lower visibility than industry giants.
Additionally, while some authors consider the platform the most user-friendly on the market, others find it less intuitive, making it a matter of personal preference.
Apple Books
Apple Books is a popular platform for those looking to tap into Apple's broad audience. It is also an excellent choice for authors who want to distribute their ebooks or audiobooks across the Apple Ecosystem.
Pros
One of the platform's advantages is full distribution and integration across iOS devices. Other benefits include non-exclusive distribution and attractive royalties (45-70% of the list price, depending on your chosen sales channel and pricing model).
Cons
Apple's Ecosystem is undeniably large yet still smaller than Amazon and Audible, leading some authors to opt for platforms with more comprehensive audiobook selections.
Final thoughts
We hope this article serves as an informative and actionable guide for authors looking to publish
AI audiobooks
for listeners worldwide to enjoy and appreciate.
If you're looking for a reliable and comprehensive platform to publish and distribute your audiobook, consider the Audiobook Creative Exchange (ACX), Findaway Voices, Kobo Writing Life, Google Play Books, Author's Republic, and Apple Books.
Looking for a way to bring your audio book to life? Hiring a traditional voice actor to record your audiobook is expensive and cumbersome, making it hard for new and self-published authors to tap into this lucrative medium.
Instead, AI tools like ElevenLabs make recording an audiobook fast and accessible, and it all starts in our Voice Library. Check out the library and record your first audiobook today using Projects. Interested in creating your own audiobook?
Create an AI narrator with our AI Audiobooks tools
.
FAQs
What factors should I consider when choosing a platform for publishing my audiobook?
When choosing a platform for audiobook publishing, consider the following factors: audience reach, royalty rates, exclusivity requirements, distribution options, marketing support, and ease of use.
What is the advantage of choosing a platform with non-exclusive distribution options?
A key advantage of choosing a publishing platform with non-exclusive distribution options is the ability to distribute your audiobook across several platforms, allowing you to reach a wider audience.
How do royalty rates vary among different publishing platforms?
Depending on your distribution model and sales channel, royalty rates can vary across different platforms. While some audiobook publishing platforms offer a list price percentage, others offer flat royalty rates.
Is choosing a platform with a larger market share better, even if it means accepting exclusivity requirements?
The answer to this question depends on your priorities and goals. Although platforms with larger market shares like ACX provide you with better reach and visibility, they often require exclusivity, which limits distribution options (and vice versa for platforms with smaller market shares).
How important is marketing and promotional support when choosing an audiobook publishing platform?
Depending on your goals, marketing and promotional support availability can be crucial or less critical. If you plan on promoting your audiobook through other platforms, lacking such tools shouldn't be too much of a headache.

Boost user satisfaction rates by implementing dynamic conversation flows with sentiment analysis

parameters and voice selection
Increase user engagement by combining text and voice interfaces in your chatbot
Building a chatbot that simply works isn't enough anymore. Today's users expect conversational AI that sounds natural, understands context, and responds with human-like speech. Yet many chatbots still feel robotic, leading to frustrated users and failed interactions.
The key? To combine conversational AI with the right
Text-to-Speech
technology.
This article explains how. Whether you're building your first intelligent chatbot or improving an existing one, these practices will help you create the most effective
conversational AI voice agent
possible.
Understanding the basics
Natural language processing serves as the backbone of modern chatbots. Unlike simple rule-based systems, NLP helps
chatbots
understand context, tone, and subtle variations in human language. The best chatbots use machine learning models trained on millions of conversations to recognize patterns in user inputs and generate appropriate responses.
Getting NLP right matters because it directly impacts user satisfaction. When your chatbot accurately understands user intent, it can provide relevant answers quickly. Modern NLP models can detect sentiment, extract key information, and even understand idioms or colloquial expressions. This sophistication makes conversations feel natural rather than mechanical.
Text-to-Speech technology adds another crucial layer. Modern
TTS
systems have moved far beyond robotic voices, using neural networks to generate speech that mirrors human conversation patterns. The right TTS solution can convey emotion, adjust speaking pace, and even include natural pauses—all essential elements of engaging dialogue.
Planning your chatbot strategy
Success starts with knowing your audience. Before choosing any technology, map out who will use your chatbot and what they need. Are they technical users comfortable with artificial intelligence? Or do they need a more straightforward user interface? Understanding your target audience shapes every decision that follows.
Next, set clear goals for your conversational AI solution. Define what success looks like—whether that's reducing support tickets, increasing user engagement, or handling specific types of queries. These goals help you choose the right conversational AI platform and measure performance effectively.
Language support needs careful consideration. If you serve users in multiple regions, plan for different languages from the start. Modern chatbot platforms can handle multiple languages, but you'll need to consider how
Text-to-Speech
works for each one. Some languages may need specialized voice models for natural-sounding speech. Try
Eleven v3
, our most expressive text-to-speech model yet.
Technical requirements deserve equal attention. Consider:
Integration with existing systems
Scalability needs
Data privacy requirements
Response time expectations
Voice quality standards
The right planning prevents costly adjustments later. Take time to document requirements, test different platforms, and gather feedback from stakeholders. This groundwork ensures your chatbot meets both user needs and business goals.
Designing natural conversations
The difference between a good chatbot and a great one lies in conversation design. Natural dialogue flows don't happen by accident—they need careful planning. Start by mapping common user journeys and identifying key interaction points. Each conversation should have a clear purpose while staying flexible enough to handle unexpected user inputs.
Sentiment analysis plays a crucial role in making conversations feel human. Your chatbot should recognize when users are frustrated, confused, or satisfied and adjust its responses accordingly. This might mean changing its tone, offering more help, or smoothly transferring to a human agent when needed.
Voice assistants
need special consideration in conversation design. Speaking is different from typing—users tend to be more verbose and use more natural language when talking. Design your dialogue flows to handle longer, more conversational inputs. Include confirmation sounds and verbal acknowledgments to show the system is listening and understanding.
Integrating Text-to-Speech
Converting text to natural speech requires careful planning and the right technical approach. While the technology has improved dramatically, creating natural-sounding interactions still demands attention to detail. Here's how to implement TTS effectively in your chatbot:
Step 1: Choose your voice technology
Start by selecting a TTS provider that matches your quality requirements and budget. Test several voices with your target audience to find the right fit. If you need a unique brand voice, consider voice cloning technology. Make sure your chosen solution supports all languages your chatbot will use.
Step 2: Optimize speech parameters
Configure your speaking rate to match natural conversation pace. Create custom dictionaries for accurate pronunciation of industry-specific terms. Set appropriate pause lengths between sentences to mimic human speech patterns. Implement proper emphasis for questions and statements. Find the right balance between voice stability and emotional expression.
Step 3: Handle real-time delivery
Implement audio streaming to reduce initial response time. Set up proper buffering to prevent audio gaps or stutters. Monitor and continuously optimize system latency. Create robust fallback systems for handling poor network conditions or connection issues.
Step 4: Test and refine
Run comprehensive tests for pronunciation across different content types. Verify proper handling of numbers, dates, and special symbols. Test response quality under various network conditions. Collect and analyze user feedback about voice quality. Monitor system performance as you scale up usage.
Step 5: Maintain and improve
Keep pronunciation dictionaries updated with new terms and corrections. Regularly test new voice models as they become available. Monitor performance metrics and optimize based on data. Collect and analyze user interaction data to identify areas for improvement.
Technical implementation
Getting the technical details right ensures your chatbot can handle real-world conversations smoothly. Natural language understanding forms the core of your system, converting user inputs into actionable data. Whether users type or speak, your system needs to accurately capture their intent.
Start with your language model selection. Consider these crucial elements: Your chatbot needs strong intent recognition to understand what users want. It should handle entity extraction to pull out key information like dates, names, and numbers. Add sentiment analysis to gauge user mood and adjust responses accordingly. Build in language understanding that covers your users' common expressions and industry terms.
Training and tuning require careful attention. Feed your models with high-quality conversation data focused on your use cases. Set up continuous learning to improve accuracy over time. Create feedback loops that help your system learn from both successes and failures.
Testing and optimization
Success comes from constant refinement. Start by gathering detailed user feedback through multiple channels. Track key metrics like completion rates, error frequency, and user satisfaction scores. Monitor conversation flows to spot where users get stuck or frustrated.
Build your testing framework around these key areas: Language understanding accuracy - Check if your chatbot correctly interprets user queries Response appropriateness - Verify that answers match user intent Voice quality - Test speech clarity and natural sound Conversation flow - Ensure smooth dialogues without dead ends Error handling - Confirm proper management of unexpected inputs
Make improvement a continuous process. Remember that optimization isn't just about fixing problems—it's about enhancing what already works well. Look for opportunities to make good conversations even better. Test new features that could improve user experience. Stay updated with the latest advances in
conversational AI
technology.
How to create a conversational AI chatbot with ElevenLabs

Build your knowledge foundation:
Upload relevant documents, add website URLs, or input specific text content. The system processes this data to create accurate, contextual responses that align with your business needs.
Perfect the voice:
Fine-tune how your chatbot sounds. Select from ElevenLabs' voice library or create a custom voice.
Test and evaluate:
Put your chatbot through real-world scenarios. Use the built-in testing tools to make practice calls and assess performance.
Implement and monitor:
Add your chatbot to your platform using ElevenLabs' widget. Copy the widget ID and integrate it into your website. Customize the appearance to match your brand's look and feel.
Final thoughts
Businesses can now build conversational chatbots that not only understand and respond intelligently but do so with natural, engaging voices. Success comes from getting the fundamentals right. Strong natural language processing ensures your chatbot understands users correctly.
Well-designed conversation flows keep interactions smooth and purposeful. Quality text-to-speech integration makes every interaction feel more human and engaging. When these elements work together, the result is a chatbot that truly enhances the user experience.

FAQs
How do voice-enabled chatbots handle different user interactions and speech patterns?
Modern chatbots combine speech recognition tools with natural language processing (NLP) to understand various spoken words and accents. They convert speech to text, analyze the user's intent, and use chatbot analytics to improve understanding over time. The system gets better at handling different speech patterns through continuous data collection and learning.
Can chatbots integrate with existing social messaging platforms and business systems?
Yes, today's chatbot platforms support integration with Facebook Messenger and other social messaging platforms. Most chatbot implementations can connect with existing data systems, customer databases, and business tools. This creates seamless chatbot conversations across all your communication channels.
How do you measure chatbot performance and track user satisfaction?
Track key metrics through chatbot analytics, including successful user interactions, completion rates, and user inquiries handled. Monitor chat bot performance through data collection of user feedback, conversation length, and issue resolution rates. This helps optimize the chatbot's predefined responses and improve overall customer experience.
What's the difference between text-based and voice-enabled chatbot conversations?
While text-based chatbots only process written text, voice-enabled chatbots use speech recognition tools to handle voice commands and spoken words. They create more natural human conversations by combining speech to text technology with conversational interfaces. This leads to more engaging user interactions and better customer satisfaction.
How do you start with chatbot development and chatbot implementation?
Begin by choosing a reliable chatbot platform and defining your user's intent patterns. Focus on proper data labeling and entity recognition to understand user inquiries accurately. Create clear conversational interfaces, test with real user interactions, and continuously educate users about the chatbot's capabilities. Regular analysis of chatbot performance helps optimize the virtual assistant over time.

What does a video game voice actor do?
Video game voice actors use their voices to bring characters to life in games. They work with game developers to understand the characters they're playing and then deliver their lines to convey emotions and personalities.
Whether they're voicing heroes, villains, or side characters, their job is to make the game's story more immersive and enjoyable for players. They may also make sounds like grunts or screams during action scenes. Overall, voice actors are key to making games more exciting and memorable.
The 5 best video game voice actors
Being a great video game voice actor is a real skill. Some of the most prolific voice actors renowned for their iconic characters include:
1. Troy Baker
- An American voice actor known for his roles as Joel in "The Last of Us" and Booker DeWitt in "BioShock Infinite," among many other characters.
2. Ashley Johnson -
Notable for her portrayal of Ellie in "The Last of Us" and Gwen Tennyson in various "Ben 10" games.
3. Nolan North -
Renowned for his performances as Nathan Drake in the "Uncharted" series and Desmond Miles in the "Assassin's Creed" franchise.
4. Jennifer Hale -
Recognized for her notable roles as Commander Shepard in the "Mass Effect" series and FemShep in "Mass Effect 3," as well as having voiced various characters in "World of Warcraft" and "Overwatch."
5. Laura Bailey -
Known for her portrayal of Jaina Proudmoore in "World of Warcraft," Fetch in the "Infamous" series, and Abby in "The Last of Us Part II," among other roles.
The downsides of using video game voice actors
While traditional voice actors bring undeniable talent and emotional depth to video games, there are several drawbacks to consider.
Firstly, hiring professional voice actors can be significantly more expensive than using AI, particularly for games with extensive dialogue or multiple language versions. The process can also be time-consuming, from auditions and contract negotiations to scheduling recording sessions.
Additionally, maintaining consistency in voice performance over long development cycles or multiple game installments can be challenging if a voice actor becomes unavailable.
Lastly, the inflexibility in modifying recorded dialogue can pose constraints in late-stage game development, potentially leading to compromises in narrative or character development.

AI voices work for both small and big games.
In short, AI voices are cheaper, faster, and more flexible for game development.

Few providers offer as high a level of control over their AI voices—users can fine-tune each character's voice based on emotion, expression, dialect, and language. In addition, voices are trained to be as human-like as possible, taking into account intonation, pauses, and speech style.
Cons
Cost:
Starting at $31/month per user, PlayHT is one of the most expensive AI voice generation tools on the market, limiting its affordability for individuals or indie developers.
Teething problems:
The PlayHT 2.0 model is still in Beta, and users have experienced some errors and issues with accuracy when using the software.
Intonation issues:
Several users report issues with intonation and non-verbal utterances, which can add a time burden to developers using the tool to generate large amounts of character speech.
Pricing
PlayHT does offer a free plan, but it’s limited to online usage and only allows for 5,000 free words per month.
Professional plans currently start at $31.20/month.
Rating
4/5
5. Synthesia
Synthesia is primarily an AI video generator. However, it has recently added a built-in text-to-speech function to its wheelhouse, allowing creators to generate natural-sounding voiceovers.
Pros
Diversity:
Synthesia offers 400 different male and female voices in 120+ languages. You can also use SSML tags (Speech Synthesis Markup Language) to fine-tune realistic accented voices.
Previews:
The software allows for a preview of the AI voice narration, before taking the time to download the generated audio. This is helpful for a streamlined game development workflow.
Helpful instructions:
The Synthesia website offers a host of helpful support tools and explainers, ensuring picking up the new software is as easy as possible for new users.
Cons
Slow generation:
Users report that it can take several minutes to search the library for a suitable AI voice. This could pose a problem for developers hoping to quickly turn around new games.
Pronunciation issues:
Synthesia’s model can’t pronounce all words, and sometimes needs the user to input phonetic spelling, which could become a real time-suck for developers generating large volumes of NPC speech.
Not tailored to gaming:
This voiceover software is mainly used for corporate scripts, meaning it’s unlikely to be well-suited for more creative uses, like video game production.
Pricing
After a free trial of some simple demo features, subscriptions to Synthesia range from £23-£69/month [or approx. $29-87/month], making it one of the more expensive options.
Rating
2/5
6. Murf.ai
Murf.AI is one of the fastest-growing AI software providers out there. They offer 120+ text-to-speech voices in 20+ languages, and an all-in-one AI voice generator along with voice cloning tech.
Pros
Easy to use:
Murf.ai’s ‘All-in-one’ voice generator is designed for optimal user experience.
Quality:
Voices generated by Murf software are realistic and high-quality, good for injecting games with industry-quality character voices.
Customization options:
Murf’s voice cloning and generation software has strong customization features including adjustable pitch and speed.
Range of use cases:
Murf’s AI voices have found a range of successful use cases—from e-learning to advertising and podcasts. Their versatile tools are well suited to creative uses like game design.
Cons
Low-quality languages:
The model is yet to be able to synthesize non-English voices to the same quality as English ones, posing issues for high-quality game dubbing.
Audio issues:
Many users report issues with the voice generation software, especially glitches in the customization tools.
Cost:
Again, Murf.ai provides another software that don’t come cheap. To have free reign across their suite of audio editing features, you’ll need a paid plan, which starts from $23/month.
Pricing
A Creator starter plan will cost you $23/month, while a fully comprehensive business plan increases to
$79/month.
Rating
3/5
7. Listnr
Listnr is a Generative AI Engine that uses a library of 1000+ voices to create voiceovers, along with offering voice cloning capabilities.
Pros
Rapid generation:
Listnr’s Text-to-Speech engine works in seconds, bringing huge time benefits to game developers
Trusted software:
Listnr’s quick and sleek software has gained them over 1,000,000 users worldwide
Game-specific capabilities:
Among use cases in sales and social media, podcasts, and YouTube content, Listnr creates authentic voices designed specifically for game characters.
Cons
Robotic voices:
Listnr’s voices are not ideal for expressive, emotive game characters as they can often sound flat and robotic.
Not many non-English language accents:
While Listnr can provide voices in 63 US English accents, other languages are more limited—Japanese speakers can choose from 13 accents, while only 2 accents are available in Arabic.
Pricing
Users can get 20 downloads/exports per month and 1GB storage for free, or upgrade to Student ($5/month), Individual ($19/month) or Solo ($39/month) price plans.
Rating
2/5
How to choose the perfect NPC voice generator
When selecting your NPC voice generator, bear the following considerations in mind.
Avoiding robotic speech
Synthetic speech varies in its ability to recreate the work of real voice actors. While tools like Listnr are good for corporate presentations and voiceovers, engaging NPC voices need to be expressive, emotive, and characterful.
ElevenLabs'
text-to-speech tool
,
for example, personalizes each character's voice, taking into account their narrative role, personality, and background. These characters will respond with life-like emotion as the storyline unfolds, each maintaining consistency in a unique tonal quality and personality.
Global reach
If you’re hoping to capture the imagination of gamers worldwide, it’s critical to make sure your NPCs will sound at home in a variety of languages. Some platforms offer a range of languages, but differences in dialect that would be obvious to a native speaker are left lacking. On the other hand, tools like ElevenLabs can generate authentic, life-like speech in
28 languages
.
Creative control
NPCs can provide a high level of creative control for game developers—these characters can be personalized by the game creators in every aspect, especially voice. ElevenLabs' synthetic voices can be customized to adapt accent, language, emotion, and speaker profile. The more you can fine-tune character voices and adapt them to different situational contexts, the more lifelike, engaging, and exciting a collection of NPCs can be.
Time-efficiency
NPC speech generation can be an incredibly time-consuming process—the more NPCs you want to create, and therefore how fleshed-out and engaging your game will be, the greater this time-suck. AI tools present the opportunity for game developers to turn months into seconds, so it’s important to consider how rapid, easy to learn, and easy to adjust your character voice model would be.
Final thoughts
AI voice generators like ElevenLabs, Replica Studios, and Speechify enable game developers to animate NPCs with striking, lifelike voices, enhancing narrative depth and player immersion. These technologiesoffer vast voice libraries, multilingual support, and customizable features, optimizing NPC dialogue for emotional resonance and global reach.
With the perfect voice generator for NPCs, developers can ensure narratives are rich, engaging, and accessible, all while cutting costs and labor-intensiveness in their development workflow.
As the demand for more interactive and immersive games grows, selecting the ideal voice generation platform becomes crucial, shaping the future of storytelling and game development.

Better leverages ElevenAgents to build Betsy and make AI assisted loans accessible
Last updated
Mar 14, 2026
•
7 minutes reading time
Authors
Lauren Rothwell
, Growth
Doubling lead-to-lock conversion rate and reducing origination costs by 41%.
On this page
Introduction
Mortgage origination is time-intensive and requires licensed advisors
Who is Betsy?
Why ElevenLabs
How financial institutions can benefit from the Tinman AI and ElevenLabs stack
Impact and results
What’s next
Learn More
Contact Sales
Better is an AI-native mortgage lender that has funded over $110 billion in loan volume powered by its proprietary mortgage and home equity platform, Tinman. Its operation runs the Tinman AI Platform, Better’s full stack mortgage platform that stores all loan application facts in one comprehensive data structure. In June 2025, Better adopted ElevenAgents to extend Tinman’s digital mortgage workflows through Betsy, the first voice-based AI loan assistant built for the mortgage industry. Betsy uses a professionally licensed, consented cloned voice so every interaction stays on brand.
Unmute
Mortgage origination is time-intensive and requires licensed advisors
Mortgage origination requires state-licensed consultants whose time is scarce and costly. Much of that time is consumed by repetitive qualification calls, outbound dialing, and follow-ups. Those servicing costs must be recovered in the economics of origination and ultimately influence the mortgage rates that can be offered.
For most financial institutions, the biggest obstacle is fragmented systems: eligibility, pricing, and servicing data sit across multiple LOS, CRM, and internal tools. Because their data is scattered across multiple point solutions, they often struggle to deploy AI in a meaningful way across their mortgage operations. Tinman was built to solve this fragmentation issue: the platform acts as a unified system connecting these tools through a governed context graph.
Who is Betsy?
Betsy is the generative AI component layered on top of Tinman and is able to access its proprietary loan engine. Originally, Betsy was only able to tap into a full mortgage application and answer mortgage application inquiries through a chat function.
Using ElevenAgents, Better has programmed Betsy to verbally communicate with borrowers and streamline the mortgage application process through a voice agent. Credit pulls, pricing, and rate locks can be initiated by voice through ElevenLabs, with Tinman executing each step and returning the results. Controls are explicit: pricing and eligibility are computed by Tinman and communicated by the agent, with no unsanctioned decisions. Regulated steps - including credit pulls, locking, authentication, and transfers to humans - require consent and follow state licensing requirements.
Orchestration runs inside Better’s environment via an MCP-based multi-agent system connected to Tinman tools. Calls reach a single public ElevenAgents endpoint, while internal agent switching and tool execution happen within Better’s stack. The design keeps determinations in Tinman and uses ElevenLabs Agents as the controlled voice interface.
On the consumer side, Better uses Tinman and ElevenAgents to run an AI voice-based loan assistant that completes eligibility checks, pricing, and rate locks over the phone. By shifting repetitive servicing work from licensed consultants to the agent, Better lowers its cost to originate and passes that efficiency into more competitive rates for borrowers. Tinman’s scenario math helps increase approval rates by exploring options that human loan officers would not have time to compute, while the cloned “Betsy” voice delivers a consistent, natural experience across every conversation.
ElevenAgents has helped us to build the first AI voice-based loan assistant of its kind for the mortgage industry. By layering Betsy's voice on top of the Tinman platform, we’ve been able to 2x our lead-to-lock conversion over the last year. Betsy allows us to approve more borrowers, and move them through the mortgage experience while maintaining consistency with Better’s brand.
- Vishal Garg, CEO, Better
Listen to the experience
(snippet of simulated call, no real customer data):
00:00
/
00:00
Why ElevenLabs
Better initially launched its voice offering using a Speech to Speech model, but chose to move to a pipeline stack combining Speech to Text, an LLM, and Text to Speech with ElevenAgents to achieve a more natural, lower latency experience with better control and reliability.
Another key aspect of Better’s decision to choose ElevenLabs as its conversational agent partner was the platform’s stability under high tool-call volume, with each customer conversation potentially triggering dozens of Tinman tool calls. For financial services, where each interaction spans multiple systems and regulatory steps, this level of stability is a prerequisite, not a nice to have.
ElevenLabs gives us the control and reliability we need to handle over 100,000 monthly mortgage conversations, each triggering dozens of Tinman tasks. We needed a platform built for stability at enterprise scale.
- Cory Hayden, AI Product Manager, Better
Better and its Tinman AI partners also needed unique brand voices for their agents. ElevenLabs voice cloning technology enabled professionally licensed, consented clones of contracted voice actors to serve as the agents’ voices so every interaction felt natural and reflected each lender’s brand as intended.
How financial institutions can benefit from the Tinman AI and ElevenLabs stack
Beyond Better’s consumer offering, the same Tinman and ElevenAgents stack is available to mortgage lenders, banks, credit unions, and fintechs that leverage Tinman’s SaaS platform. Mortgages are traditionally a broken process - often made up of eight different systems and 28 different people involved in a single journey. Tinman centralizes the knowledge base, rules, pricing, and workflows in one place so partners can launch branded voice agents that originate more mortgages end to end without the need to build their own agent orchestration or integrations into mortgage systems.
Tinman AI runs the same balance-sheet optimization logic Better uses internally so partners can offer highly competitive rates, consolidate existing debt, and win competitors’ customers by paying off other loans into a single, better-structured mortgage.
When our partners plug into Tinman AI and ElevenAgents, they can increase their origination volume and approve more borrowers while maintaining their current headcount. When there’s no need to increase operational overhead, they win against other lenders in the space by creating a competitive advantage: offering the most optimized rates to their borrowers.
- Vishal Garg, CEO, Better
Impact and results
ElevenAgents powers nearly
100,000 monthly calls
for Better,
automating 35.5% of mortgage inquiries end to end
. In 2025, Betsy placed 1.89 million outbound and inbound phone calls
saving our loan officers over 1,666 hours of human time each month
.
These time savings have compounded across multiple teams, and reduced the number of calls Better’s loan officers must make to follow-up with borrowers to complete rote tasks. Instead, Better loan officers can now dedicate their time to building trust, solving complex cases, and helping borrowers make meaningful financial decisions.
For Better.com’s consumer business, automation has:
Reduced average cost to originate by 41%
Increased lead-to-lock conversion by 100% in 2025
Enabled more competitive borrower rates by passing operational efficiency into pricing.
By shifting routine conversations and outreach to voice automation, licensed consultants and bank staff focus on higher-value advisory work, while borrowers and partners benefit from faster decisions and better economics.
What’s next
Better will expand agent-led outbound coverage across new states and acquisition sources, trigger reactivation when market rates change, and route qualified interest to state-licensed consultants. In addition, Better plans expand the AI voice-based agents capabilities to include operational assistance that will help borrowers beyond rate lock. By giving agents the ability to help assist borrowers complete tasks required to fund their loan and making outbound calls to assist borrowers in hitting key timelines to finish their loan, they’ll begin to play a role in the mortgage experience from rate lock to funding. The objective is to keep shifting routine mortgage work to agents, compressing servicing costs to provide more competitive pricing for borrowers.
On the SaaS platform side, Better plans to extend Tinman AI-powered voice agents to more partners, enabling them to launch branded voice loan officers of their own without rebuilding mortgage orchestration to achieve the same operational and cost-savings efficiencies that Better has been able to actualize in their operations.
Disclaimer: All regulated actions are performed with borrower consent and in compliance with state licensing and federal mortgage regulations, with licensed advisors engaged where required. Results described are based on internal analyses and may vary depending on borrower profile, market conditions, and loan characteristics.

More than technology
A certification hub with a challenge
School leaders are under pressure to understand how artificial intelligence can support teaching and learning. The information exists, but it’s often scattered across frameworks, case studies, prompt guides, and policy briefings.
AiED Certified is now the home for the UK’s AI in Education Certification,

backed by a clear framework, guidance, and a secure evidence portal. Alongside this, the site still provides access to its legacy library of more than 250 curated resources, including case studies, prompt guides, and policy briefings.
While these materials are no longer directly browsable, the ElevenLabs-powered voice agent has knowledge of the full archive and can be asked about it. The aim was to refocus the site on the certification framework while keeping the resource collection available through a more intuitive, conversational interface.
Voice as an interface
To achieve this, AiED Certified embedded a conversational voice agent—powered by ElevenLabs—across the new site. Instead of clicking through menus or guessing keywords, users can now ask directly:
"What are the five elements of the framework?"

"Do you have a case study about using AI to support SEND in schools?"
The agent responds instantly in a natural, human-sounding voice, surfacing the right part of the certification framework or retrieving relevant items from the resource library.
It turns complexity into clarity, helping busy school leaders get the information they need in seconds.
See the AiEd conversational agent in action
Unmute
Why this matters for access, inclusion, and reducing workload
For educators with visual impairments or reading difficulties, voice navigation lowers barriers. For colleagues newer to AI or from diverse linguistic backgrounds, it reduces the friction of jargon and unfamiliar structures.
By bridging the new certification content with the retained resource archive, the ElevenLabs voice agent helps every user find the right guidance at the right time.
For school leaders, speed to clarity matters. Instead of paging through long documents, they can ask the agent and jump straight to the relevant framework criterion, evidence exemplar, or case study. Senior leaders can now reach the right information in seconds, supporting quicker decision-making and smoother implementation.
Expanding access through the Impact Program
AiED Certified is using ElevenLabs tools
at no cost
through the ElevenLabs Impact Program.
This means schools with tight budgets, particularly in under-resourced areas, can benefit from advanced voice interfaces without prohibitive expense. Removing this barrier helps ensure innovation reaches the communities that need it most.
More than technology
This is about more than a new tool. It’s about:
Democratizing access
: making advanced voice technology available to nonprofits and underfunded schools through the ElevenLabs Impact Program.
Supporting inclusion
: reducing barriers caused by sight or learning disabilities, language differences, and varied levels of literacy.
Restoring time and dignity
: cutting the burden of search and administration.
Advancing equity
: ensuring under-resourced schools aren’t left behind.
Projects like this are reshaping how people interact with complex information online. As voice technology becomes more natural and accessible, it’s changing how we learn, search, and make decisions. This shift goes beyond convenience. It represents a new standard for access: faster, clearer, and more human.
With ElevenLabs, AiED Certified has turned a static resource hub into a voice-enabled guide—creating a more accessible path to safe, effective, and ethical AI adoption in every school.
For organizations that manage a large library of resources or multi-page frameworks, embedding a conversational
voice agent
could make a real difference—helping visitors get the right information instantly, by asking rather than searching.

Bibliothèque Sonore Romande
Bibliothèque Sonore Romande (BSR) was founded in Lausanne, Switzerland in 1976 with a single goal - ensure that people who cannot read printed text can still access books and knowledge.
They serve blind, visually impaired, and reading-disabled audiences across the French-speaking world, with a catalog of more than 38,000 titles.
BSR operates with a team of 10 people, supported by a large network of volunteers and funded through public subsidies and private donations. As a non-profit foundation, every franc saved on production goes directly back into accessibility.
How ElevenLabs is used
BSR uses ElevenLabs Studio to produce audiobooks from EPUB files in French.
Over the past year, this has enabled:
20 full audiobooks.
11 issues of local magazines.
10 official Swiss public voting guides.
Where ElevenLabs makes a difference
Feedback from subscribers and professional partners has been consistent - the quality is comparable to human narration.
As one listener put it:
"We would never have believed this level of quality would be available so soon."
This level of quality expands what can be produced, especially in cases where traditional workflows fall short.
Time-sensitive content
Some materials require fast turnaround. Swiss public voting guides have legal deadlines, and educators often request books with little notice.
With ElevenLabs, production timelines are reduced from weeks to days, making it possible to deliver critical information on time.
Difficult-to-produce content
Other materials are consistently underserved due to the nature of the content:
Long legal texts.
Technical documents.
Repetitive or low-demand publications.
These are difficult to assign to volunteer narrators. With ElevenLabs, they can be produced reliably, with consistent quality and no fatigue constraints.
You can listen to samples here:
https://www.bibliothequesonore.ch/rechercheBSR/lecteur/Voxia
What comes next
BSR is expanding its catalog by combining volunteer-led production with AI-generated titles.
Volunteers already produce around 800 titles each year. With ElevenLabs, access to books and essential information is no longer constrained by narrator availability.
This ensures that more people can access not just literature, but also the information they need to participate fully in society.

If your nonprofit organization could benefit from ElevenLabs technology, check out our Impact Program page for more information about how to apply.

From now on, selected BILD podcasts will also be available in English, thanks to a new collaboration between BILD and ElevenLabs. This partnership allows BILD to expand its primarily German-language audio offerings to include more languages, using both ElevenLabs’ AI and Axel Springer’s in-house developed audio AI, aravoices.
Among the first English-language offerings generated for BILD using ElevenLabs are the current episodes of the successful podcast series
RONZHEIMER.
and
FC BAYERN INSIDER
, which are of particular interest to an international audience. The episodes which use synthetic voices are transparently labeled as AI-generated and appear on the podcast portals in a separate playlist dedicated for the formats, like on BILD.de, Amazon
Music
,
Apple Podcast
,
Spotify
and everywhere where podcasts are available.
Listen to the German & English renditions of the shows below:
Ronzheimer [English]
Ronzheimer [German]
Bayern Insider [English]
Bayern Insider [German]
Claudius Senst, CEO BILD-Group, had this to say “At Axel Springer, we are actively exploring the possibilities and opportunities where and how we can strengthen journalism and expand our digital reach using artificial intelligence. At the end of 2023, for example, we launched Hey_ at BILD, an AI helper that has already answered over 45 million questions since then. Through the cooperation with ElevenLabs, we now want to test for BILD how we can make suitable audio content with a personalized voice even more attractive for an English-speaking audience.”
“We are delighted to be working with BILD, Germany’s largest media brand”, says
Mati Staniszewski
, co-founder at ElevenLabs. “BILD podcasts can now reach more people globally, bridging language barriers and improving accessibility. And because our AI preserves the original voices and style in translation, audiences worldwide can now experience podcasts such as Paul Ronzheimer’s in their own languages, delivered in their creators’ authentic style.
Axel Springer’s audio AI aravoices generates over 2 million audio streams per month for BILD and WELT
Starting in 2020, BILD and WELT already have specific synthetic brand voices that were created by Axel Springer’s proprietary audio AI aravoices. With the help of these brand voices and a fully automated distribution process, aravoices generates and publishes over 2 million audio streams per month for both brands. The aravoices offering not only boosts audio usage and increasing monetization through audio advertising, but also provides barrier-free access to journalistic content. BILD alone now publishes up to 40,000 audio articles per year, which are used for a variety of formats such as the read-aloud function on BILD.de, playlists on Spotify and Apple Podcasts as well as Alexa News Update.
Anne Küpper, Director Product & Engineering at Axel Springer, added “With aravoices, we developed our own impressive AI technology at Axel Springer at an early stage, which we use to set journalistic articles from BILD and WELT to audio in real time and distribute them successfully. Many positive user comments show the popularity and success of the audio streams with our listeners. Thanks to the cooperation with ElevenLabs, we can now expand our brand voices with specific, lifelike author voices.”

At this year’s GreenBiz conference, an annual event for corporate sustainability professionals to discuss hands-on initiatives to fight climate change, there was one speech that stood out from the rest.
Bill Weihl, founder of
ClimateVoice
and a long time corporate sustainability leader, highlighted the impact that vocal employees within companies have on climate policy, by speaking up so companies step up. Corporations can play a vital role through their actions and their influence on shaping public policy, but the majority are failing to hit their climate goals and are silent on policy. To change this, Bill joined with other sustainability leaders to launch
the LEAD statement
, already signed by hundreds of sustainability professionals, to raise their voice for policy action.
Bill, who lost his own voice to ALS, delivered his powerful speech using ElevenLabs. Bill and his colleague Sharon created an Instant Voice Clone using samples from speeches he gave in the past. Surprised and pleased by how much the Instant Voice Clone resembled his real voice, they gathered and cleaned up 3 hours of audio to create a Professional Voice Clone that sounds just like him.
While Bill is not one to brag about his own impact, his ClimateVoice team shared that Bill’s speech brought an in-person audience of thousands (and a much larger digital audience) initially to tears and ultimately to a standing ovation. Watch a recording of Bill’s speech here:
To learn more about how you can join Bill and the ClimateVoice team in their fight for climate policy progress, check out
their website.

Looking ahead
BLACKBOX AI is pioneering a new category of enterprise software - fully autonomous, voice-first agents that manage everything from coding to infrastructure without human bottlenecks.
Today, they power over 30 million developers across two primary voice enabled products, Logger and Robocoder.
Logger autonomously monitors systems 24/7, detects issues, and calls on-call engineers to explain incidents, propose and implement fixes in real time.
Robocoder

helps teams build full-stack applications from scratch: front-end, back-end and even AI-powered applications with no API keys required, through natural, conversational interfaces.
Challenge
As a leader in deploying fully autonomous coding agents at global scale, BLACKBOX AI faced a unique challenge: how to make those agents feel truly human.
Before adopting ElevenLabs, BLACKBOX AI experimented with multiple AI providers, including OpenAI, to build conversational interfaces for their agents. However, they encountered three key limitations:
Unnatural conversations, leading to lower user engagement.
A limited set of only 10 voices, restricting multilingual and locale-specific use cases.
High costs at enterprise scale
Why BLACKBOX chose ElevenLabs over OpenAI
After A/B testing the two providers, ElevenLabs stood out as the only one that could match BLACKBOX AI’s standard for natural, contextual, low-latency voice interactions. In particular, BLACKBOX AI chose ElevenLabs for three main reasons:
Superior conversational quality:
Users consistently preferred ElevenLabs voices in A/B testing, with higher adoption and engagement. Natural turn-taking and more realistic delivery made conversations flow more smoothly than with other providers.
Global voice coverage:
ElevenLabs supports a significantly wider selection of voices - more than 5,000 compared to OpenAI’s 10 - across different languages and accents. This breadth ensures more accurate, natural interactions globally.
Scalable cost-effectiveness:
ElevenLabs offers a pricing model that makes large-scale deployment feasible, an important factor for a company like BLACKBOX AI that powers over 30 million users.
We A/B tested OpenAI’s and ElevenLabs’
voice agent
offering and found that usage was better with ElevenLabs. Conversations felt more natural and the voice selection across different languages mattered.
– Robert Rizk, Co-Founder & CEO at BLACKBOX AI
Implementation
BLACKBOX integrated ElevenLabs Agents across two products to enable the following capabilities:
Logger
24/7 monitoring of server logs.
Autonomous phone calls to on-call engineers when incidents occur.
Conversational troubleshooting with clear context and proposed fixes.
Authorized remediation to reduce downtime.
Robocoder
Voice-driven ai coding agent across IDE, WhatsApp, and phone.
Real-time code explanations for faster onboarding and knowledge transfer.
Creation of AI voice apps, enabled by ElevenLabs APIs.
Results
Voice-first workflows are now a core part of BLACKBOX AI’s product experience:
Engineers resolve incidents faster with real-time conversational alerts
New devs onboard quicker via voice-guided codebase explanations
Usage, retention, and developer satisfaction have all increased
Looking ahead
BLACKBOX AI sees voice-first agents as the next wave of enterprise software. Logger and Robocoder are only the beginning - the company plans to expand into more multilingual, real-time, and large-scale deployments powered by ElevenLabs, in line with its mission to remove human bottlenecks and accelerate innovation in software development.

.

We’re excited to announce a partnership with

Bookwire is an internationally leading technology provider in the digital publishing sector. Based in Frankfurt, the company serves thousands of publishers in producing and distributing ebooks, audiobooks, podcasts, and other digital publishing products.
We are partnering with Bookwire to bring ebooks from their publishers' catalogs to life through dynamic narration, making titles that were previously only in text available in audio. We are proud to join forces with one of the most innovative and advanced voice AI companies, combining ElevenLabs’ groundbreaking AI technology with Bookwire’s expertise in digital distribution.
